_comment: THE single source of truth for the session model (CLAUDE.md §21). Before 2026-09-18 these windows existed as six hand-kept copies -- the table in docs/architecture/session-model.md §2, Python literals in scripts/journal.py session_of(), a `const SESSIONS` array in scripts/chart.js, a `const KZ_WEIGHT` map beside it, the `session` enum in schemas/trade-file.schema.json, and the weight table in session-model.md §3 -- with no generator and no drift test between any of them. §21 asks for sessions that are configurable and historically reproducible; a markdown table is neither. scripts/sessions.py is the ONE reader, scripts/sync-sessions.py regenerates the derived spots, and scripts/tests/test_sessions.py fails the build on drift. Adding or changing a session = edit THIS file, run `python3 scripts/sync-sessions.py --write`, done.
_rationale: The WHY of every number here -- why the windows are these windows, why asia is 20:00-00:00 New York, why metals get a full London weight and crypto never gets one -- stays in docs/architecture/session-model.md, which this file does not duplicate. That document is the decision record; this file is the machine-readable form of its conclusions.
_version_why: Bumped whenever a window, zone, weight or gate changes. A session label is stamped on every journalled trade, so changing a window silently re-labels history: a trade recorded as `ny_am` under one model and `off` under the next is the same trade with two different facts attached. CLAUDE.md §11 wants a configuration snapshot to be able to say WHICH model produced a label, and §59 treats a session-rule change as potentially Trading System version significant. Bump this and the label stops being ambiguous.
_reference_clock_why: session-model.md §1. Windows are defined in the opening market's own clock and converted to UTC for the date in question, so they follow daylight saving. A fixed UTC hour is correct in summer only -- the 08:30 America/New_York macro release is 12:30Z in winter and 11:30Z in summer.

sessions._comment: `start`/`end` are local hours in `zone`, end-exclusive, and may cross midnight (end <= start means the window runs into the next local day). `precedence` breaks a tie when a timestamp falls in more than one window and a caller needs ONE label; lower wins. It is declared here rather than left to the order of an if/elif chain, which is how an overlap gets silently resolved (CLAUDE.md §19's objection, applied to sessions). `display` is the short label the chart legend draws; it is here so the page and the journal cannot disagree about what to call a window.

london.what: London open through the LBMA morning gold fix (10:30 London)

ny_am.what: US macro release time (CPI, NFP, EIA) through the first 90 minutes of the equity session

ny_pm.what: Afternoon session into the equity close

asia.what: The decks' own Asia killzone; used for Asian-session high/low liquidity levels and for journalling. Chosen by measurement 2026-09-12 (docs/backtests/2026-09-12-asia-session.md), not by convention.

_off_label_why: The label for a timestamp inside no window, and the one every gate below falls back to. It is named here rather than spelled 'off' in five files because it is also the trade-file schema's enum member and the journal's grouping key.

weights._comment: Weight CLASS per (asset_class, session). The class -> points mapping is NOT here: it is analysis-params.json timing.weight_by_class (full 7 / reduced 3 / none 0), which is the scoring parameter and the tuning surface for /improve. Keeping the class here and the points there is what lets a weight be retuned without touching the session model, and vice versa. asset_class comes from instruments.json display.<sym>.asset_class, defaulting to the market.
weights._default_why: An asset class nobody has weighted earns no timing credit. Defaulting to `reduced` would hand free points to every instrument added after this file was last considered.

gates._comment: Conditions under which NO session credit is awarded, whatever the clock says. session-model.md §4.

weekend._why: Python weekday(): 5 = Saturday, 6 = Sunday, evaluated in UTC. Crypto trades weekends, metals and indices do not, and the gate applies to ALL of them -- the sessions these windows name are not running for anyone, so a Saturday 09:00 London is not a London session.

gates._min_timeframe_why: Not copied here. It is a SCORING gate (below 15m, no timing credit) and it already lives beside the points it gates. A session is still a session on a 1m chart; what it stops earning is credit.
